newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 12.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 12.4 pct.

text.p: The average Croatian money market rate edged down 30 basis points to 12.4 percent on Thursday in slow trade.
Dealers said the banks' accounts were full ahead of monthly salary and pension payments which should soon reduce the amount of money on offer. They put Thursday's supply at 70 million.
Daily settlements halved to 21.8 million kuna from Wednesday amid dwindling demand.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 14.5 million kuna half of which were call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent.
Term loans were struck at rates ranging between 11 percent for five and seven day funds and 18 percent for two-month borrowings.
Insurers rolled over previous 11-day funds at steady nine percent and two-week loans at 15 percent.
The banks charged 15 percent for old one-month loans and 18 percent for two-month borrowings.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrate firmer at 6.1716 against the dollar and at 3.5730 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
